text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate observed for public API (api.redwood.ai) from EU customers via Cloudflare edges. Auto-escalation -> paging oncall-net and oncall-sre. See monitors: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/5432

oncall-net: Looking. Seeing DNS resolution timeouts and SERVFAILs from a subset of resolvers in eu-west. Traceroutes show queries hitting Cloudflare then timing out.

oncall-sre: I'm seeing a spike in origin 5xx in us-east-1 but latencies are normal elsewhere. Could be traffic misrouted?

eng-reliability: Quick context: we use GeoDNS (third-party) with weights + Route53 health checks + Cloudflare as CDN. If the GeoDNS weights got skewed traffic can concentrate on one region.

miguel: Confirmed: GeoDNS dashboard shows a scheduled automation run 04:22 UTC that recalculated weights. It pushed 82% traffic -> us-east-1 for latency profile. That aligns with when errors started.

aisha: Who triggered the automation? deploy-bot or scheduled job?

deploy-bot: automation-job-weights v2 executed by cron at 04:22 UTC. Change log id: CW-2026-04.

oncall-net: Cloudflare edge logs (sample):
```
CF-Request-ID: abc123
Upstream: 502 from origin
Edge-Error: resolver_timeout
Resolver: 1.1.1.1 -> SERVFAIL
```
Looks like upstream resolver failures combined with concentrated traffic towards us-east increased load + evictions -> origin 5xx.

lina-cs: CS reports multiple customers in EU seeing errors when hitting app, some on enterprise plans. We should update status page.

oncall-sre: Mitigation plan: 1) Lower GeoDNS weight to spread across regions; 2) Lower DNS TTL to 60s to force re-resolve; 3) Temporarily failover us-east pool if health-check flapping continues; 4) Notify Cloudflare and AWS support. Executing 1 & 2 now.

miguel: Command I'm running:
```
# update geo weights via provider API
curl -X POST https://geodns.example/api/v1/weights -d '{"us-east": 30, "eu-west": 35, "ap-south": 35}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

oncall-net: Done. Confirmed new weights accepted. Propagation depends on resolver TTLs. Lowering our authoritative TTL for api.redwood.ai -> 60s (was 300).

miguel: Route53 snippet ran to adjust record TTL for fallback records:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://failover-ttl-change.json
```
Change submitted: change id C0ABCDEF.

aisha: Reached Cloudflare support (ticket CF-7892). They confirm intermittent resolver timeouts in eu-west edges correlated with recent config push on their side. They're rolling a fix.

oncall-sre: Good. While we spread traffic, I'm also removing the automation cron temporarily to prevent re-run during incident.

eng-reliability: Note: our GeoDNS health-check relies on DNS-level pings. If Cloudflare edge resolvers return SERVFAIL, the GeoDNS health-checks might incorrectly mark healthy regions as unhealthy and re-weight. We'll add a guard.

product-ops: Status page draft: "Partial outage impacting EU customers: DNS resolution errors and increased 5xx. Mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m." Approve?

lina-cs: Approve. Push now.

oncall-net: Status page updated. Also posting to #customers-enterprise a short note.

oncall-sre: Short term metrics: error-rate dropped from 9% -> 2.1% in last 6m after reweight and TTL change. Still elevated but trending down.

miguel: Cloudflare updated: edge fix deployed to eu-west at 04:38 UTC, they report resolver stability improving. Ticket updated.

aisha: We're seeing some clients still stuck because of long-lived resolver caches at their ISPs. Workaround: advise customers to flush DNS or switch to 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 temporarily. CS team notified.

eng-reliability: Next steps: 1) Re-enable automation with improved guard: require 3-minute sustained health signal before re-weighting. 2) Add resolver error rate as input to GeoDNS decision. 3) Postmortem and RCA. Assignments: miguel -> implement guard, jamie (eng-reliability) -> postmortem draft, aisha -> customer comms follow-up.

product-ops: Are there any billing-impacting customers? Lina, CS?

lina-cs: Two enterprise customers had errors on high-priority endpoints; ops engaged directly, they accepted a credit offer.

oncall-net: Handoff: I'm going offline in 10m. oncall-sre taking lead for next 6h. Please escalate to eng-reliability if we see reversion.

oncall-sre: Taking lead. Will monitor and coordinate with Cloudflare + Route53.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity -> Partial outage (S2). Affected region: EU. Impact: DNS resolution failures, elevated 5xx. Mitigation: GeoDNS reweight + TTL lowered + Cloudflare edge fix. Next update in 20m.

miguel: I've disabled automation cron with id cron-weights-v2. Will push guarded version in staging and run canary.

eng-reliability: Quick checklist for post-incident: timeline, automation decision logic bug, resolver dependency blindspot, customer impact summary, corrective actions, and follow-up dates. Let's aim to publish postmortem in 72h.

lina-cs: CS notes: customers appreciated speed of comms. One asked for a network-level SLA clause. Logging that with sales.

oncall-sre: Monitoring: setting an alert to trigger if EU resolver SERVFAIL rate > 0.5% for 3m.

product-ops: Thanks all. Solid run. :thumbsup:

aisha: leaving a reminder: add unit test for automation logic + integration test that simulates edge resolver SERVFAIL to prevent unsafe reweights.

eng-reliability: Agreed. Assigning Miguel for fix; ETA 48h for code + tests.

oncall-net: Closing chat for now, will reopen if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
